newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 28.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The government has given a clear signal that the state is prepared to privatise shares in the four largest Czech banks held by the state. The first of the banks to be privatised is, as expected, IPB. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik was entrusted with forming a team to oversee the privatisation of the bank as soon as possible, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- According to a national survey, 40 percent of Czech citizens believe the crown will remain stable in the coming year while 41 percent expect the crown to weaken slightly.
- The price of fuel will remain the same next week in spite of speculation that they may rise following the fire in Ceska Rafinerska's Litvinov refinery at the weekend.

- The Skoda automobile plant will manufacture between 2,000-5,000 Octavias by the end of this year, according to Evzen Krauskopf from the company's press department. The majority of these vehicles will be sold domestically.

- Czech Railways has received a 200 million mark loan from Germany's Kreditanstalt fur Weideraufbau, according to Rudolf Mladek, the general manager of Czech Railways. The funds will be used to modernise the railway corridor between Breclav and Ostrava.

- The Czech National Bank's foreign exchange reserves reached $12.66 billion at the end of October, a slight increase of $30 million from the end of September. This breaks the trend of the previous three quarters when the reserves decreased. An increase is expected in November as well.

- The city of Prague is planning to reconstruct the Congress Centre, previously known as the Palace of Culture, in order to host the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in the year 2000.

- The management of Motokov expect a net profit of 10 million crowns on a turnover of 3.8 billion crowns, an increase of one billion crowns over the year before, according to Pavel Blaha from Motokov.
- Shareholders of Aero Holding may sue representatives of Aero Holding if a government plans to erase Aero Vodochody's debt is approved in tomorrow's general meeting.

PRAVO - Just over half the Czech population is for membership in the EU, according to a national survey from IVVM. This is an increase of nine percent from March, 1996. The percentage against EU integration decreased to 26 percent while those who do not know increased to 23 percent.
- Ceskomoravsky Penzijni Fond posted a profit of 70 million crowns in the first ten months of 1996, according to the press spokesman for Investicni a Postovni Banka, Jan Rezek.
